title: Adding a prefix adds one observer, not every node that carries it
body: Typing a prefix into Add Prefixes In Locked Cluster ticked every node with that prefix. When a prefix resolved to more than one node, both went into the estimate, from positions that can be tens of km apart, and pulled the answer between them. It now adds the same node the automatic de-duplication kept, says when there was more than one to choose from, and leaves the swap to Resolve on map. A prefix you already picked yourself is left alone.

title: Finishing on the map applies what you picked
body: Swapping which node stands for a prefix on the map only ticked a box in the Step 2 list; until you scrolled back and pressed Apply Inside Locked Cluster the map kept showing the old pick. “Done resolving” now applies the picks, along with any weight you changed, and says so. Leaving the cluster instead, with Choose Another Cluster or by switching to a rival region, still applies nothing.

title: A repeater on a roof gets its real antenna height
body: The line-of-sight check assumed every observer's antenna at 12 m. When a cluster is locked the tool now looks up, in 3D BAG, the tallest building within 50 m of each observer; those get its roof plus a 3 m mast, the others keep 12 m. The cluster status says how many, and an observer's popup shows its antenna height and how far that roof is. Netherlands only, like the terrain check.

title: Fresh visits start in the right place
body: What's new showed old entries because the browser kept yesterday's file; the page now revalidates on every visit. A fresh visit puts the cursor in the first-hop field, also right after the intro. And a Step 2 label no longer shows before a cluster is locked.

title: A shared link now carries the whole scene
body: Share used to send only Step 1; whoever opened the link landed on the candidate list and started over. It now also carries the region you chose, the observers you ticked off or reweighted, a repeater you dragged, a proven link you removed, which estimate you ran, the layer switch and the relief slider, each only when you changed it. Opening the link replays all of that and says what no longer applies. The address bar follows along, so copying it gives the same link as the button.

title: Choosing a region shows what it is waiting for
body: Picking a region pulls proven links from mc-radar for up to 14 nodes, which takes a few seconds. The page now shows the same loading overlay a shared link uses, saying which region it is pulling links for, until the cluster is locked.

title: Ranges, links and heat can be switched off
body: Once a cluster is locked, three chips above the map switch the range polygons, the proven links (with their arrows and support nodes) and the heat on or off. On a phone the ranges and links start off, because on a small map they covered the answer in one pink wash; the clue zone, the tied region and the observers always stay.

title: Easier on a phone
body: The map no longer traps the page: one finger scrolls past it, two fingers pan it, and on a desktop the wheel zooms it with ctrl held, with a hint from the map. After you find regions, choose one or run an estimate, the page scrolls to what changed. The attribution box no longer covers a third of a small map, the top bar takes two rows instead of three, the icon buttons and the relief slider are bigger to tap, and the spam-detector import is folded under one line so the first-hop field comes first.

title: Drag an observer to where it really is
body: Upstream positions are advertised, and sometimes stale or wrong. While resolving on the map you can now drag an observer to correct it. The advertised spot stays as a hollow marker with a dashed line to the new one, the estimate is invalidated until you re-run it, and that observer's proven-link range is set aside because its link distances were measured from the old spot. Put it back from its popup, or all of them with Reset positions. Nothing is saved between visits.

title: Terrain refinement looks across the whole likely area
body: Refine with Terrain + LOS used to re-score only the 36 best cells of the flat estimate, so a spot that terrain would have favoured but that ranked 37th or lower could never come up. It now also samples the area that ties with the best cell, every 2nd cell or wider so the pass stays under 150 cells, and the status line says how many cells it saw.

title: Resolve on map shows the rival regions, and can undo
body: Each candidate region now says how many of its prefixes also resolve in another region, on the cards and in the popup, so you can see how much there is to choose. While resolving on the map, the other regions from the same search stay outlined; tap one to switch to it. Picks you changed can go back to the automatic choice, per prefix from the popup or all at once with Reset picks in the banner.

title: What's new opens on screen on a phone
body: On a phone, once a cluster was locked and the Resolve on map button appeared, the bell dropped to a line of its own at the far left and the What's new panel opened off the left edge of the screen. The help and bell buttons now stay together at the right, and on a narrow screen the panel opens as a sheet at the bottom of the screen.

title: The estimate now says how sure it is
body: The status line used to say 'typical error 2 km' for every estimate. It now says how far the evidence allows the target to be, as 'likely within X km', and what share of the searched area scores the same as the best spot. When that share is 40% or more it says the observers do not pin the target down, and when every observer sits on one side it says from which direction a new observer would help. The heat on the map now covers the whole searched area instead of the 36 best cells, and the dashed outline is the area that ties with the best cell.

title: A region wider than 30 km ranks lower
body: With the larger cluster radius, unrelated repeaters that share a prefix could chain into one wide candidate region that outranked the real one on size. A region wider than 30 km, the longest range the tool assumes for any observer, now has its score scaled down by how far it exceeds that. On the accuracy fixture this fixes the two cases it hit and changes no other.

title: Load an incident straight from the spam detector
body: Step 1 now has a list of recent incidents from mc-spamdetector.nl and a field for an attack URL or number. Picking one fills the first-hop prefixes with the incident's entry hops, weighted by packets, and finds the region, which used to mean reading the table off the attack page and typing it in. A link with ?incident=2047 does the same.

title: Cluster km starts at 12 instead of 6
body: Two observers of the same node often sit more than 6 km apart, so a 6 km cluster radius split them into separate regions unless a 2nd-hop node happened to bridge them. The default is now 12 km, the same distance the tool assumes a repeater hears. On the accuracy fixture that gives 8 more cases an estimate when only 1st-hop prefixes are entered, and the error goes down in both modes. You can still type any radius.

title: An observer's range is its longest proven link
body: An observer's assumed range came from the 80th percentile of its proven link distances, which left 133 of 823 observers in the accuracy fixture with a range shorter than the distance they actually heard the target at. It is now the longest plausible link, capped at 30 km for the estimate. Median error on the fixture goes from 1.9 to 1.7 km and the 90th percentile from 11.5 to 9.9 km. The likelihood surface is flatter as a result: fewer cells stand out, which is honest about what the evidence pins down.

title: The cluster's shape comes from 1st-hop observers
body: The cluster centre, the yellow region, the span on the candidate cards and the area the estimate searches now follow the 1st-hop observers. 2nd-hop observers still show, still join a cluster and still set an observer's range, but they no longer move its centre or stretch its outline.

title: 2nd-hop observers no longer pull the estimate
body: A node that heard the target at 2 hops was scored as if the target sat within 10 km of it. It is not: the target is within reach of some relay that is within reach of that node. 2nd-hop observers still show on the map and still shape the cluster, but the estimate now uses 1st-hop observers only, and the status line says how many were left out. On the accuracy fixture the median error goes from 2.3 to 2.0 km.

title: Step 1 is the first thing you see
body: The buttons and the relief slider sat above Step 1, pushing the thing you actually came to do down the page. They are now below the three steps. Map popups were also white on white; fixed.

title: One map instead of two
body: The old flat map has been removed; everything now draws on the 3D map, which still opens looking straight down. One map engine to load, and no more features that only exist on one of them.

title: The map is the 3D one now, lying flat
body: The tool now opens on the 3D map, looking straight down. It tilts once an estimate is ready.

title: Relief slider moved off the map
body: The relief slider sat on top of the map it was adjusting. It now lives in the controls card.

title: Tilt the 3D view all the way to the horizon
body: The 3D view now tilts to a near-horizon angle, which is what shows you a blocking ridge.

title: The 3D view finally has hills in it
body: The 3D view now shows real elevation, exaggerated six times so Dutch relief is visible, and says by how much.

title: Pick between same-prefix repeaters on the map
body: Two repeaters can share a prefix. Resolve on map shows the one the tool did not pick; click to swap it in, then Apply.

title: Sharper estimates from a softer idea of coverage
body: Coverage now fades with distance instead of stopping at an edge. Typical miss drops from 2.9 km to 2.4 km.

title: Places the height data cannot see no longer win by default
body: Spots the height data cannot see no longer beat spots it checked and found blocked. Inland, nothing changes.

title: Cluster cards are readable again
body: The step 2 cluster cards were green-on-green and barely readable. They are now dark tiles with a green edge on the one you picked.

title: Better line-of-sight checks, and honesty about the gaps
body: Line of sight now uses proper diffraction maths and the earth's curve, and says so when the height data does not reach.

title: Says when a duplicate repeater was picked by guesswork
body: Where no proven link decides between two same-prefix repeaters, the tool guesses the nearest one and now says how often.

title: Estimates no longer look more precise than they are
body: Positions were printed to the metre but land a median 2 km out. Now three decimals, with the typical error beside them.

title: Coverage now based on what a repeater can hear
body: Coverage counted outbound-only links, which run longer and made it too generous. It now prefers inbound evidence.

title: Ignoring impossible repeater links
body: Links too long to be a single hop are now ignored, and the tool says how many.

title: Sharper estimates from overlapping observers
body: Observers are now combined by where they all agree, rather than letting the loudest outvote the geometry.

title: Range and confidence outlines drawn correctly
body: The shaded outlines around ranges, clusters and the estimate were collapsing to a line. Fixed.

title: Repeater lookups working again
body: Prefix searches had stopped reaching MC Radar and were falling back to a thinner source. Fixed.

title: A short guide for newcomers
body: First-time visitors now get a walkthrough of the three steps and the tuning controls. Reopen it anytime with the ? button.

title: Share a link to your search
body: A Share button copies a link to your current clues, so you can hand someone the exact search instead of describing it.

title: Cleaner map controls
body: Buttons no longer float on top of the map. Clear Map and the 3D toggle now sit together above Step 1.

title: Shareable links
body: Step 1 can now be pre-filled from a URL, so other sites can link straight into a result instead of a blank form.

title: Smarter clustering
body: Repeaters heard through a relay (2nd-hop) are now included based on real network links where available, not just a flat guessed range.

title: Duplicate-node fix
body: Switching between duplicate nodes for the same prefix no longer silently resets the weight you'd set.

title: New top bar
body: Added a Dutch MeshCore-branded top bar with links to the community site, Mesh-Hunter, MC-Radar, and this project's GitHub.

title: Tighter default search radius
body: Cluster search radius now defaults to 6km instead of 50km, matching typical real-world repeater density.

title: Docker deploy
body: One-command deploy via Docker Compose with a built-in Cloudflare Tunnel sidecar.
